Abstract: Monitoring autonomous large language model (LLM) agents for covert malicious behavior is challenging due to delayed, context-dependent, and long-horizon attack patterns. title: LGMT: Logic-Grounded Metamorphic Testing for Evaluating the Reasoning Reliability of LLMs
description:

Existing evaluations rely on static benchmarks, which fail to assess robustness under logically equivalent transformations and often overestimate reasoning capability. description:
arXiv:2605.24004v1 Announce Type: new

title: How Much Thinking is Enough? Quantifying and Understanding Redundancy in LLM Reasoning
description:
arXiv:2605.23926v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reasoning-capable large language models solve hard problems by emitting long chains of thought, paying heavily in latency, GPU time, and energy. Casual inspection of their traces reveals extensive reformulation, verification, and circular self-reflection, yet how much of this deliberation is actually necessary has never been measured at scale or explained from first principles.
